summary.decisions: Used a regenerateWorld callback (registered via setRegenerateWorld) so lifecycle.js stays pure and unit-testable; update.js owns the world and the collision world rebind. startGame only rerolls when ctx.areaContext is provided (bare startGame in unit tests doesn't reroll). continueRun sets h.checkpoint to the level entry (HERO_ENTRY_X=100, HERO_ENTRY_Y=500-h.h) before h.respawn() so the hero lands at area -1, not the death spot. retryFromGameOver delegates to startLife (a life start) rather than restoreArea, per lifecycle.md §3.
summary.done: Fixed all 5 reviewer findings for task 1.2. (1) BLOCKER: retryFromGameOver now calls startLife (a life start) instead of restoreArea — restores the full area arrangement, places the hero at the area entry with full energy and i-frames, and does NOT restore lives (per lifecycle.md §3). (2) MAJOR: continueRun now re-positions the hero at the level entry (area -1) via h.checkpoint = {x:100, y:500-h.h} before calling h.respawn(), so continuing from 2-3 lands the hero at 2-1, not the death spot. (3) MAJOR: retryFromGameOver no longer assigns lives directly; startLife is the single owner of the life-start semantics. (4) MAJOR: startGame now invokes a registered regenerateWorld callback (set via setRegenerateWorld) to re-roll the generated world with fresh random choices for a genuinely new game; death and Continue never call startGame so they never reroll. (5) MAJOR: removed the hardcoded hero.lives = GAME_RULES.startingLives from retryFromGameOver. Added resetHeroTransient() helper to lifecycle.js to clear death flags/energy/i-frames before respawn. Added 6 new tests to lifecycle.test.js covering fresh generation, continueRun re-positioning, resetHeroTransient, and startLife clearing leaked state. All 18 lifecycle tests pass; full suite 93/94 (only the known Space-jump pause flake remains).

summary.done: Fixed all 4 round-2 BLOCKER findings for the shared area-entry screen + death flow. (1) Boss zone entry id: updateBoss now sets hero.currentArea = LEVEL_DEF.checkpoints.length (one past the last flag) so showAreaEntry's (currentArea-1) offset maps onto the level's boss area and displays '1-B' instead of '1-4'. (2) Boss zone restart point: updateBoss now sets hero.checkpoint to the last (boss) flag position BEFORE showing the entry screen, so confirming it (startLife -> hero.respawn()) lands the hero beside the boss checkpoint. (3) AREA_ENTRY->PLAY hook: added from!==S.AREA_ENTRY to the SELECT->PLAY guard in update.js so confirming the entry screen no longer calls startGame (no hero rebuild / generation reroll). (4) Entry flag re-trigger: startLife now latches the entry flag (the one hero.checkpoint points at, matched on x since flags are x-distinct) to triggered=true after restoreArea re-arms all checkpoints, so the next overlap frame is a no-op per checkpoints.md §1. Updated the 'death in 1-3' test to assert the entry flag is latched while other flags re-arm; added a boss-zone integration test asserting areaId '1-B' and respawn beside the boss flag; made the 'new game' test start from a valid HOME state so its SELECT transition is well-formed.
summary.lessons_learned: The 'new game shows entry screen' test was silently depending on the BLOCKER-3 bug: with state leaked at AREA_ENTRY, the buggy startGame re-fire happened to push it back to AREA_ENTRY, so it passed only because of the defect. Fixing the defect exposed the latent state-leak; the fix is to make the test start from a valid pre-SELECT state (HOME), not to preserve the buggy behavior. Verify re-trigger fixes by stepping the real update loop (U.update) for many frames and asserting state stays PLAY, not just by checking the latch flag.
summary.tradeoffs: Matching the entry flag on x only (not x+y) is robust to the hero's body-offset y stored in hero.checkpoint, and flags are x-distinct so the match is unambiguous. Setting currentArea one past the last flag (checkpoints.length) for the boss zone is a display-only convention (currentArea is only read by formatAreaId); the boss respawn point comes from hero.checkpoint, not currentArea.
summary.decisions: Kept the formatAreaId area-index contract (area >= checkpoints.length-1 -> boss) intact and instead corrected the call-site currentArea value, so existing formatAreaId tests remain valid. Latched the entry flag in lifecycle.startLife (the single owner of the respawn placement) rather than special-casing the collision handler, keeping the update.js checkpoint handler uniform. summary.tradeoffs: Legacy corridor kept (as LEGACY_CORRIDOR + LEVELS[0].LEGACY + deprecated generateLevel()) because full runtime rewiring to the zone model is task 7.1. The zone model is now the authoritative structure the runtime references (hero.zones, exported levelZones + getActiveZone()), but the camera still clamps to the LEGACY corridor length until 7.1 swaps it. Vertical zones have a bottom platform at bounds.y+bounds.h and a one-way top platform at VERTICAL_TOP_PLATFORM_OFFSET=56.
summary.lessons_learned: Screen-coordinate gotcha: y=0 is the TOP, so a bottom (entry) flag has a LARGER y than a top (exit) flag. The R1 code had this inverted (entry at y=452, exit at y=1572) which was geometrically wrong. zonePlatforms must receive the full zone object (with orientation) to branch correctly — passing bare {bounds} silently produced horizontal geometry for vertical zones.
summary.done: R2 fixes for task 2.1. The zone model is no longer dead code; it is the authoritative structure the runtime references. MAJOR (R2#2): Fixed flagY for vertical zones — entry flag now at the BOTTOM (y = bounds.y + bounds.h - flagH = 1572, largest y) and exit flag at the TOP (y = VERTICAL_TOP_PLATFORM_OFFSET - flagH = 8, smallest y). Fixed zonePlatforms for vertical zones: bottom supporting platform at bounds.y+bounds.h (full width) + one-way top platform at y=56 (120px wide, under the exit flag). Updated zone.test.js assertions to match correct screen-coordinate semantics (entry.y > exit.y). Updated docs: structure.md §4 (coordinate summary table) and checkpoints.md §1 (screen-coordinate clarification).

summary.lessons_learned: The zone model (task 2.1) and the clear sequence (task 2.2) had divergent area indexing conventions: the zone model uses -1..-4 while the clear sequence used legacy 0..3. This caused getActiveZone() to resolve incorrectly after the first clear. The fix required mapping legacy checkpoint indices to zone-model areas at the checkpoint handler boundary. The entry flag y-position differs for vertical zones (bottom platform) vs horizontal zones (ground), so beginClearFadeIn must use the zone's entry flag y rather than a hardcoded ZONE_GROUND_Y.

summary.lessons_learned: Double-jump reach = ground apex (jump^2/2g) + double apex ((0.85*jump)^2/2g): Scarlet ~143px, Balthazar ~101px, so tier steps must be <= ~85px (101 - 16 margin) to be comfortable for the weaker hero. node --test on a bare .js file runs fine (no package.json, ESM default).
summary.done: Created petal-panic/js/terrain.js: a pure terrain grammar + seeded per-game RNG. createRng(seed) is a mulberry32 PRNG (numeric or FNV-1a-hashed string seed) with next/int/pick/float, so the same seed always yields the identical generation stream. BLOCK (1w, heights 1/2/3, solid, ground-rising, not one-way) and PLATFORM (widths 1/2/3, tiers 1/2/3, one-way, one thickness, not solid) grammars + makeBlock/makePlatform factories. doubleJumpReach/minHeroDoubleJumpReach/maxClearableStep derive tier spacing from the real hero physics (GRAVITY 1500, double-jump 0.85 factor, Balthazar is the binding weaker jumper) so each tier step is reachable by both heroes with a 16px margin; tierToOffset maps tiers 0..3 to equal-spaced pixel offsets. Added terrain.test.js (21 tests).
summary.decisions: mulberry32 for the PRNG (small, deterministic, platform-stable). Tier spacing is derived from hero reach by construction rather than a hand-tuned constant, so the 'reachable by both heroes' invariant holds automatically; Balthazar (smaller jump) is the binding constraint. Units model (not pixels) so 3.2 owns pixel layout. RNG is a stateful closure; determinism comes from fixed seed.
